chunks: Ibn Mahbub, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: concerning

Regarding a slave who wounds two men, he said: “He is shared between them if his offense encompasses his value.” It was said to him: What if he wounds one man at the beginning of the day and wounds another at the end of the day? He said: “He is between them both so long as the wālī has not yet passed judgment regarding the first wounded man.” He said: Then if he commits an offense after that? He said: “His offense is upon the last one.”

key_terms.الْأَخِيرِ: the last person in sequence, upon whom the later liability falls
key_terms.الْوَالِي: the authority or ruler who issues judgment
key_terms.جِنَايَتُهُ: his offense or injurious act carrying legal consequence
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: an enslaved person whose legal liability is being discussed

ai.seo_question: How is liability determined if a slave injures more than one person in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about liability when an enslaved person injures multiple people. It explains how responsibility and entitlement are shared between the injured parties, and that the ruling may change once the wālī issues judgment in the first case.
